verdictSummary: The source-only decision is the right call and it does discharge the recorded P0-AUDIENCE blocker in substance: no wire-bearing type names the full IContract or the remaining market, so no grant scope can carry them, and a P0 producer can now be implemented without leaking to restricted guests. But the delta's central load-bearing factual claim -- that envelopeOf is the SINGLE narrowing and that EVERY read path already goes through it -- is false in the current worktree: the grant-projection path, the first surface the decision itself names, narrows inline at projectCampaignStreamForGrant.ts:252 and never calls envelopeOf. That falsity is not cosmetic: it makes the new SHALL ('every wire read path SHALL obtain campaign events through it') a requirement the code currently VIOLATES with no task admitting the fix, and it makes task 6.3's 1:1 falsification row vacuous for the grant leak rows. Two further SHALL overreaches (GM 'exactly the same wire facts'; 'SHALL NOT appear on a grant-projected delivery item' versus the delivered eventDigest, which commits to the payload) and one release-condition collision with the pre-existing P1 requirement need narrowing. All edits are text-level; none disturbs the decision itself.

findings.detail: SUBSTANCE: the blocker is resolved. P0-AUDIENCE asked for 'an explicit source-only OR field-projection prerequisite'; D12 elects source-only, records the alternative as rejected with four grounds, and preserves the compact guest fields. P0-UNDEFINED is answered by the conditional-absence paragraph. P0-TEST-BOUNDARY is answered by scoping replay to contract-only and disclaiming materialization of unrelated non-contract missions. Because the private payload is an envelope sibling and no wire-bearing type (ICampaignAuthoritativeState, any ICampaignEvent payload, ICampaignGrantDeliveryItem, the room-code snapshot) names it, a restricted guest cannot receive the full contract even at the grant surface -- so a P0 producer CAN now be implemented without a leak. SURFACE TRACE: (a) grant projection -- narrows, but INLINE at :252, not via envelopeOf; (b) applyCampaignEvent shared state -- folds only event.payload, which never carries the private field; (c) room-code guest hydration -- receives already-narrowed ICampaignEvent[] and delivery items, so it is structurally downstream and cannot see an envelope at all; (d) genesis snapshot -- built by the compact wire builder, unchanged. FULL SWEEP of stored-row access: grep -rn 'payload\.campaignEvent' src/ returns exactly two non-test production sites, JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:180 (inside envelopeOf) and projectCampaignStreamForGrant.ts:252. Every other consumer -- campaignActivityRoute, rewind-preview, GmCampaignImpactDerivation, CampaignReplacementReplay, CampaignRetroactiveCorrectionCommit, CoordinatedOutcomeCorrectionRun/Target/steps, campaignShadowParityRunner, campaignSnapshotBackfill, campaignLegacyAdoption, campaignAuthorityMigration, campaignCombatOutcomeInbox -- contains NO '.payload' access at all and reaches events through envelopeOf-backed helpers. So there is exactly ONE bypass, and it is the most safety-critical surface in the whole decision. CONSEQUENCE: the leak does not exist today (the inline read narrows to the same single field, so the effect is identical), but three things the delta asserts are wrong. (1) 'the single narrowing' and 'every read path goes through it' are false. (2) The structural argument 'deleting the narrowing is a single reviewable line and a single test' is false -- it is two lines in two files, and the grant one is the one a reviewer is least likely to be watching. (3) The new SHALL at spec.md:127 ('every wire read path SHALL obtain campaign events through it') is a requirement the code VIOLATES as of this base, yet task 6.1 instructs the implementer to leave envelopeOf 'unchanged so every wire read path stays compact by construction' and never names the :252 edit needed to make the SHALL true.

findings.detail: NO SILENT RE-SCOPING -- verified mechanically. The diff is +53/-0 across three files: no task is checked, no receipt, non-claim or deferral is removed or weakened, and Group 6's preamble says so explicitly and truthfully. D12 is consistent with D3 (its 'new event type with its own scope' remedy is D3's immutability law applied forward), with D10 (no dual authority, flag stays false), and with D11 (it consumes P0a's prepared transaction rather than redefining it). No canonical openspec/specs/campaign-authority exists, so there is no canonical SHALL to contradict. THREE TENSIONS FOUND: (1) DIGEST VERSUS ABSOLUTE SHALL. spec.md:125 says the private facts SHALL NOT appear 'on a grant-projected delivery item'. Every delivery item carries projectedEventIdentity: stored.eventDigest, and canonicalizeEventDigestV1's material includes payload: event.payload -- so once a private field exists, a cryptographic commitment DERIVED FROM the private bytes does appear on a grant-projected delivery item handed to restricted guests. That is not a content leak (sha256 is one-way and a preimage attempt needs the full envelope metadata too), but it is a confirmation oracle for a guessed payload and it is a literal counterexample to an absolute SHALL. The delta never mentions it. (2) GM OVERREACH. spec.md:145 asserts the GM all-scopes grant receives 'exactly the same compact wire facts' as any campaign-scope recipient. False as written: projectCampaignStreamForGrant.ts:264-266 gives an all-scopes grant CampaignSnapshotPublished rows that a restricted grant is denied, and D4 at design.md:25 independently says GM grants 'receive the raw stream (global revisions + original chain)'. The intended claim -- that grant scope does not govern the PRIVATE CONTRACT boundary -- is correct; the sentence as drafted contradicts both D4 and the code. (3) RELEASE-CONDITION COLLISION. The pre-existing requirement at spec.md:105 gates full private HTTP readback on 'until an explicit source-only audience contract exists', and spec.md:123 repeats it. D12's commit subject is literally 'admit source-only contract projection audience contract'. Read plainly, the older SHALL's release condition is now satisfied, while the new requirement at spec.md:131 denies the release. Only later-and-more-specific-wins resolves it, which is exactly the kind of ambiguity a future implementer resolves in the permissive direction. D12's prose tries to head this off ('remains blocked exactly as the P1 requirement states') but does not amend the gate itself.

The P0b red-first row is genuinely falsifiable and non-tautological: it fails before 6.1 because no private field exists, so part (a) has nothing to read, and it is pinned at a REAL SQLite close/reopen rather than an in-memory fixture. The P1 red-first row (same intent submitted twice with different expectedRevision values, expecting one commit plus one duplicate-command receipt) is a real behavioral discriminator of the command-identity rule, not a restatement of it. Worth a compile-time note in 6.1.

The private payload rides inside the journal's canonical event bytes, so it is covered by the hash chain and by any future export, backup, replay-to-another-host, or support-bundle path that copies STORED ROWS rather than narrowed events. D12 constrains READ paths only; it says nothing about bulk row copy. No such path exists today (I found none in src/), but the decision does not forbid one from being added.

reEditVerification.detail: This is the strongest of the five responses. The VALUES/commitment distinction removes the literal counterexample without weakening the requirement, the carve-out is stated positively with a new prohibition attached ('SHALL NOT expose any surface that confirms a candidate private payload against a delivered identity'), and a new SHALL pins the private field INSIDE the digest material so a future implementer cannot 'fix' the oracle by silently dropping hash-chain coverage of the private payload. The rejection reasoning -- that excluding it would leave the private facts as the only uncovered part of the envelope, and would require editing a canonicalizer shared by every stream type -- is sound and better than the neutral carve-out I proposed. The 6.3 test row that pins the commitment as EXPECTED is a genuinely good addition: it prevents a later reader from mistaking the residual for a bug.
